You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From e9380df851878cee71df5a1c7611584421527f7e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Mario Limonciello <mario.limonciello@amd.com>
Date: Sun, 31 Oct 2021 20:48:52 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] ACPI: Add stubs for wakeup handler functions

The commit ddfd9dcf270c ("ACPI: PM: Add acpi_[un]register_wakeup_handler()")
added new functions for drivers to use during the s2idle wakeup path, but
didn't add stubs for when CONFIG_ACPI wasn't set.

Add those stubs in for other drivers to be able to use.

Fixes: ddfd9dcf270c ("ACPI: PM: Add acpi_[un]register_wakeup_handler()")
Acked-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Mario Limonciello <mario.limonciello@amd.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211101014853.6177-1-mario.limonciello@amd.com
Signed-off-by: Linus Walleij <linus.walleij@linaro.org>
---
 include/linux/acpi.h | 9 +++++++++
 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+)

diff --git a/include/linux/acpi.h b/include/linux/acpi.h
index 143ce7e0bee1..668d007f0917 100644
--- a/include/linux/acpi.h
+++ b/include/linux/acpi.h
@@ -974,6 +974,15 @@ static inline int acpi_get_local_address(acpi_handle handle, u32 *addr)
 	return -ENODEV;
 }
 
+static inline int acpi_register_wakeup_handler(int wake_irq,
+	bool (*wakeup)(void *context), void *context)
+{
+	return -ENXIO;
+}
+
+static inline void acpi_unregister_wakeup_handler(
+	bool (*wakeup)(void *context), void *context) { }
+
 #endif	/* !CONFIG_ACPI */
 
 #ifdef CONFIG_ACPI_HOTPLUG_IOAPIC
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The root cause of the bug was the absence of stubs for the `acpi_register_wakeup_handler` and `acpi_unregister_wakeup_handler` functions when the `CONFIG_ACPI` configuration option was not set. This omission meant that drivers attempting to use these functions in a non-ACPI environment would encounter undefined references, leading to build failures or runtime errors. The patch adds these stubs to ensure that drivers can safely call these functions without causing issues when ACPI support is disabled.

Root cause:
The root cause of the bug was the absence of stubs for the `acpi_register_wakeup_handler` and `acpi_unregister_wakeup_handler` functions when the `CONFIG_ACPI` configuration option was not set. This omission meant that drivers attempting to use these functions in a non-ACPI environment would encounter undefined references, leading to build failures or runtime errors. The patch adds these stubs to ensure that drivers can safely call these functions without causing issues when ACPI support is disabled.
